about.acronyms: Nafath = national digital ID · REGA = Real Estate General Authority · Ejar = government tenancy registry · FAL = real-estate brokerage licence
about.metaDesc: The neutral commercial real estate exchange for Saudi Arabia, powered by SAT Real Estate (REGA FAL 1200025510).
about.title: The neutral commercial real estate exchange for Saudi Arabia, built so every figure can name its source.
about.intro: SAT Markets is an independent, neutral commercial real estate intelligence, leasing, and sales platform, starting in Riyadh. It brings together listings from owners and licensed brokers, a compliant viewing workflow, a rent index derived from the REGA Rental Index (Ejar), and a building-level intelligence map in one platform, delivered English-first with a full Arabic mirror. The platform is in preview on sample data, so the verification standard below describes how a listing will qualify at launch, not a check any preview record has already passed.
about.cardNeutralB: Open to every owner and occupier. Platform-originated stock never silently outranks owner-direct listings.
about.cardCheckedB: This is a publishing standard, not a classifieds board. At launch an owner is checked, the right to lease is confirmed, and an advertising permit is recorded before a listing can carry a verified state. Preview inventory is sample data and holds no permit, so each listing shows only the state its own record supports.
about.cardMoatB: A commercial rent index derived from the REGA Rental Index (Ejar): average rents by district and space type, minimum sample counts, and honest blanks where data is missing.
about.cardComplianceB: Designed around REGA requirements, written mandates, ad-permit gating, and data-protection and e-invoicing by design.
about.verifySub: No anonymous classifieds. The standard has three gates: the person, the right to the property, and the licence. The automated lookups behind each gate arrive before launch, so nothing in this preview has been checked against Nafath, REGA or Ejar.
about.stepNafathB: SAT reviews the person behind each listing before it publishes. Nafath national-ID sign-in, binding identity to the national digital identity, arrives before launch.
about.stepOwnerB: Owners confirm ownership and the right to lease. Automated checks against REGA (the Real Estate General Authority) and the Ejar registry arrive before launch.
about.stepBrokerB: Brokers must hold a valid FAL licence from REGA. Automated verification against the REGA register arrives before launch.
about.stepLiveB: At launch a listing publishes only after all three gates pass, and its verified state names the gate it rests on rather than standing in for all three.
about.foot: SAT Markets, commercial real estate intelligence for Saudi Arabia.

area.howTitle: What a location source has to satisfy here
area.howH: No global panel covers Saudi Arabia, and an uncontracted source publishes nothing
area.howBody: Global footfall and site-selection platforms are built for United States and European markets, so a Saudi reading has to be sourced locally. SAT will publish a mobility figure only when the source permits aggregate publication in writing, the figure carries its panel basis, aggregation count and period, and user-level output is barred by contract. Until then the numbers above stay sample data.
area.scoreBody: Each site is scored across these five lenses with the reasoning shown, never a black-box number. Works across offices, retail, mixed-use and warehouses, not just retail.
area.pdplNote: Location data is treated as sensitive: anonymised and aggregated. No on-site sensors and no personal images, ever.
area.metaTitle: Location Intelligence, Al Olaya trade area | SAT Markets
area.metaDesc: Sample trade-area page for Al Olaya, Riyadh. Every figure is sample data and no mobility or spend source is contracted.
area.srcMobileB: Not contracted, and nothing on this page comes from one. A mobility source would have to permit aggregate publication, state its panel basis and known biases, and bar user-level output in writing.
area.srcMojB: The transaction portal is a service for people to read, not a data product, so SAT does not scrape it. Calibration against real deals waits on a lawful record-level feed.
area.srcSpendB: Not contracted, and no payment or transaction data reaches SAT. A spend source would need a written agreement, a cross-border basis and a disclosure position before it could inform anything.
area.srcPublicB: GASTAT and SAMA for public context, and the REGA Rental Index (Ejar) for published rental averages with its required attribution. Averages, not medians.

rentIndex.intro: Averages of registered rental contracts, from the REGA Rental Index (Ejar). Districts without enough registered transactions are left blank.
rentIndex.cappedBody: Renewals inside Riyadh’s urban boundary are held at their last Ejar rent for five years under the Sept-2025 decree.
rentIndex.openBody: New-build and first-time leases are unaffected by the cap and continue to re-price to market each term.
rentIndex.benchNote: Every figure below is computed from a source file and traceable to it. Where a district did not clear the minimum transaction count, the cell is blank rather than estimated. Indicative, not advice.
rentIndex.tableNote: Pre-launch sample data illustrating the index mechanism. At launch, averages and bands are computed from verified closed transactions only, and thin samples are marked rather than shown. The index never prints a number it cannot stand behind.
rentIndex.trendB: We do not publish a rent trend yet. A trend needs several quarters of our own verified transactions to stand behind, and we have one quarter. Publishing a line before then would be drawing a shape, not reporting a market. It appears here when the history is real.
rentIndex.heatSubRealThin: Districts with too thin a sample are left blank rather than guessed.
rentIndex.heatSubSample: Preview sample figures. Darker is a higher average. Real district averages appear here at launch.
rentIndex.metaDesc: Saudi commercial rent figures by district and asset type, derived from the REGA Rental Index (Ejar). Averages of registered contracts, with honest blanks where the sample is too thin. Indicative, not advice.

neutrality.title: How SAT Markets stays neutral
neutrality.intro: We disclose this plainly: SAT Markets is operated by SAT Real Estate, a licensed real estate company (FAL 1200025510), and SAT Real Estate also has a licensed brokerage arm. We run the exchange so that operating it gives SAT no advantage as a broker. Neutrality here is not a slogan; it is a set of commitments you can check.
neutrality.whyBody: During this preview the platform operates under SAT Real Estate's licence, and the separation between SAT-as-operator and SAT-as-broker is contractual and operational. We are considering a separate legal entity for the exchange before public launch. We would rather be candid about this arrangement than hide it.
neutrality.closeTitle: If you ever see neutrality break
neutrality.closeBody: If you ever see SAT-as-operator giving SAT-as-broker an edge, that is a bug to fix. Tell us via the contact page.
neutrality.cRankB: SAT Real Estate publishes its own listings here, as any licensed broker does. They are marked as ours, they sit in the same ranking, and they get no placement, badge or feature another broker cannot get.
neutrality.cActT: We do not act for anyone
neutrality.cActB: SAT Markets does not represent tenants, buyers, owners or brokers. There is one path off a listing and it goes to the lister. We removed the representation service entirely rather than run an exchange that competes with the people listing on it.
neutrality.cDataB: SAT's brokerage arm gets no earlier or privileged access to leads, requirements, or index data than any other verified participant.
neutrality.cVerifB: A “verified” badge comes from an authoritative record match or a human reviewer, never from SAT choosing to favour itself.
neutrality.cReportB: We intend to publish, each quarter, what share of listings and deals were SAT Real Estate's own, so the balance is visible to everyone and not merely asserted. (Planned.)
neutrality.metaTitle: How SAT Markets stays neutral | SAT Markets
neutrality.metaDesc: SAT Markets is operated by SAT Real Estate and discloses it openly. Here is exactly how operating the exchange gives SAT no advantage as a broker.

verification.title: What a verification means here
verification.intro: Verification is a word most platforms use without defining it. This page defines it, and every label below is generated by the same code that decides what a listing page shows, so the page cannot drift away from the rule it describes.
verification.twoBody: Owner verification and listing verification answer different questions. A platform that reports one badge for both is telling you less than it appears to.
verification.ownerB: We checked the person and their ownership of this specific asset. It says nothing about whether the asset may lawfully be advertised.
verification.listingB: The asset also carries a valid advertising permit and the right to market is confirmed. This is the stronger of the two, and it is the one that governs whether a listing may be marketed at all.
verification.satB: A listing filed by SAT Real Estate itself carries neither check by virtue of who filed it. Being our own listing is not evidence about the asset.
verification.dimsTitle: The dimensions a listing record can carry
verification.dimsBody: Each dimension is checked and reported on its own. A listing is never summarised into a single word, because the single word is where the two checks above get merged. Identity is a dimension too, but it belongs to the account rather than to the asset.
verification.statesTitle: The states a dimension can be in
verification.statesBody: There are five, and two of them are not failures. Not applicable means the check does not apply to this record. Not verified means we have not established it, which is different from having established that it is false.
verification.unknownT: An unknown never becomes a known
verification.unknownB: Where we hold nothing, the surface says so in those words rather than leaving a blank, because a blank is filled in by the reader and it is filled in optimistically.
verification.collideT: Two of the five print the same words on purpose
verification.collideB: not_verified and unknown carry the same badge text, so the table above shows one label twice. That is deliberate and it is the safer of the two mistakes: a dimension we have never looked at must never read better on a listing than one we looked at and could not confirm. The raw key beside each row is what the record actually holds, and it is the one that differs.
verification.demoteBody: The flag alone is never enough, because a flag is a claim rather than a check. Five conditions are read on every record and any one of them is sufficient on its own. The third is recorded as one of two reasons, depending on whether the record names a seeding method or names no method at all. Below are the six reasons in the words the code itself returns.
verification.gateTitle: Why a listing fails the marketing gate
verification.gateBody: These are the reasons the gate itself returns. They are the same strings a listing page prints, read from the gate rather than described.
verification.todayTitle: What the records actually hold today
verification.todayBody: Stated plainly, because the alternative is a page describing a system that is not the one running. Every one of the 88 published rows is a demonstration record. All of them carry an ownership flag and an authorisation flag. None carries an advertising permit number. Of the 88, 50 record a method of seed and 38 record no method at all, and not one names an accountable checker. Nine rows state a lister relationship that contradicts the filing account. Under the rule above, no published row here passes, and every listing surface says so rather than showing a badge.
verification.noteBody: It is not a promise about future inventory and not a claim about the market. It states the rule and reports the current state of the records under it. When the records change, this page changes with them, because it reads them.
verification.metaDesc: Owner verification and listing verification are different checks. The dimensions, the states, the four demotion conditions and the current state of the records, read from the code that enforces them.

sources.title: Where the data comes from, and what we may do with it
sources.intro: Every source on this platform carries a recorded policy: whether we may store it, show it again, show something derived from it, export it, let the assistant retrieve it, and send it to an external model. The table below is that register, read at request time. It is not a summary of the register.
sources.statusTitle: What the rights status column means
sources.statusBody: Evidenced means we hold the licence or the terms that permit the use. Asserted but not evidenced means a permission is claimed somewhere and we have not put the document behind it, and the register caps that source at internal use until we do. Unknown and prohibited both cap it at nothing. The status is a ceiling, so a column can never grant more than the status allows.
sources.modelTitle: Republication rights are not model-input rights
sources.modelBody: A source we may lawfully republish is not thereby a source we may send to an external model. Those are separate permissions and the register keeps them in separate columns. Today every row records model input as never, and no external model is called at all, because the enterprise agreement that would govern such a call is not in force.
sources.neverBody: The Ministry of Justice transaction portal and the Najiz interfaces are interactive portals built for people, not data products. We do not scrape them and we will not. A platform whose whole argument is verification cannot be caught taking that shortcut.
sources.gapTitle: The gap we have not closed
sources.gapBody: The Rent Index republishes benchmarks derived from the REGA Rental Index (Ejar), and the permitted use of that source is not established. We record it as ten separate clauses rather than one question, because a statement that permits public display and says nothing about retrieval does not permit retrieval nine tenths of the way. Each clause is answered only by recording the words of a written statement, never by a tick. Until every clause carries such an answer, no figure from that source is published anywhere: not on a page, not in an export, not in a machine readable response, and not by the assistant. This is carried as an open owner decision rather than resolved in our own favour.
sources.o10CountLabel: permitted-use clauses recorded for the REGA Rental Index (Ejar)
sources.notShownTitle: What this page does not show
sources.notShownBody: Three things are held back deliberately. The internal reasoning behind a refusal quotes licence terms we are not free to republish. The stop condition and the review note are recorded in one language only, so publishing them would put English text on the Arabic page and break the parity rule. And no licensor is named on a prohibited row, because naming them would republish the term we are respecting.
sources.regNotConfiguredT: The register is not connected in this deployment
sources.regNotConfiguredB: This build carries no database credentials, so no read of the register was attempted at all. Nothing is inferred from that silence. Every source is treated as permitting nothing until its own row has been read.
sources.regReadFailedT: The register could not be read
sources.regReadFailedB: The read was attempted and it failed. That is a fault on our side and not a statement about any licence. Until it succeeds, every source is treated as permitting nothing.
sources.regNoRowsT: The register returned no rows to this page
sources.regNoRowsB: The read succeeded and came back with nothing in it. Either the register holds no rows, or this page is not permitted to read the rows it holds, and the response cannot tell those two apart. We do not guess between them. Either way, every source is treated as permitting nothing.
sources.sGastatT: GASTAT and central bank published statistics
sources.sGastatB: Official published statistics. The published terms permit republication, including commercial republication, with attribution. That is a republication right and not a model-input right, which is exactly why the two are separate columns.
sources.sRegaB: Averages of registered lease contracts, republished with attribution. SAT does not originate these figures. The derivation, export and retrieval permissions are the open gap described above.
sources.sBrokerB: Published research from commercial firms. Each publisher forbids reproduction without written permission, so the register records this source as prohibited across every use and nothing on the platform draws on it.
sources.sFsqB: Open place records used for context around a building. Redisplay and derived display are permitted publicly under the open terms; export is held to internal use.
sources.sMapboxB: Supplied under a service agreement that permits display through the service and nothing beyond it. No storage, no export, no retrieval.
sources.sPermitB: The permit lookup establishes whether a listing may lawfully be advertised. The outcome is a fact about the listing and is ours to state. The permit record itself is not republished.
sources.sNafathB: The assistant may say that an identity was checked. It may never retrieve the identity. Nothing from this source is kept beyond the outcome.
sources.sWathqB: The check outcome is a SAT fact about a listing. The deed payload belongs to the source, is not stored and is not shown.
sources.sSplB: Address normalisation. The permission is asserted from published terms, but the agreement is not on file, so the register holds this row at nothing until it is.
sources.metaTitle: Sources and data rights | SAT Markets
sources.metaDesc: The recorded policy for every data source: storage, redisplay, derived display, export, assistant retrieval and model input, with the rights status that caps each one.

bilingual.title: How this platform speaks in two languages
bilingual.intro: Arabic here is not a translation layer over an English product. Both languages are written against the same rules, and several of those rules exist because breaking one of them once cost us something. This page publishes the rules and the term base they are applied to.
bilingual.parityB: The two dictionaries must carry exactly the same keys, and a test fails the build if they diverge. That test exists because a page once shipped with a hand-written object holding both languages side by side, and the English and Arabic branches quietly drifted into two different sets of commitments. Nobody noticed, because nobody reads both columns at once. Every string on a public page now comes from the dictionaries, and a scanner fails the build on any string that does not.
bilingual.numeralsB: Arabic-Indic numerals are rejected by the Arabic linter across the whole Arabic surface. A figure a reader may need to check, copy or quote should not change shape depending on which language they opened.
bilingual.rtlB: The Arabic document is served with its own direction rather than mirrored by a style rule, so the browser lays out text, punctuation and embedded numerals the way Arabic actually reads.
bilingual.ownersT: The spelling that separates owners from angels
bilingual.ownersB: The Arabic word for property owners and a quite different word meaning angels are written with the same letters and differ by one diacritic. We always write the diacritic. A test sweeps the whole source tree for the undiacriticised spelling and fails on every occurrence, which is why the rule holds rather than merely being agreed.
bilingual.countT: Counted nouns are computed, not guessed
bilingual.countB: Arabic counts in six forms rather than two, and the boundaries fall at one, two, three, eleven and one hundred. A sentence written for one count is wrong at another, so no sentence on this platform embeds its own count. The table below is produced live by the shared formatter at each boundary, in both languages.
bilingual.countCaption: Rendered at request time by the formatter every counted sentence uses.
bilingual.avgB: They are different statistics and are never substituted for one another in either language. Where a figure is an average it is labelled an average, and the Arabic word follows the same rule rather than reaching for whichever term reads better.
bilingual.distT: A development is not a district
bilingual.distB: A planned project and an administrative district are different kinds of place, and merging them would let a project inherit a district's context and a district's figures. Both languages label them separately, everywhere.
bilingual.indexT: The index carries its source on every line
bilingual.indexB: Every reference to the Rent Index retains its attribution to the REGA Rental Index (Ejar), in both languages, and per line rather than once per page, because a line is what gets quoted.
bilingual.voiceB: The linter rejects four habits that mark translated Arabic: the auxiliary construction that replaces a direct verb with a generic verb and a preposition, the analytic possessive where an attached pronoun is the natural form, calqued marketing idiom, and the em dash, which is not an Arabic punctuation mark and is banned in the English here as well.
bilingual.termsB: The pairs below are the ones the platform actually uses, not a suggestion list. A term that renders one way on one surface and another way on the next is a defect, so the mapping lives in a single file and every surface reads it.
bilingual.metaDesc: Arabic is not a translation layer here. Enforced key parity, Western numerals, true right to left, counted nouns computed at every boundary, and the published term base.
